instance_recommendations.rationale: AMD-based equivalent of c5.2xlarge with identical vCPU/memory specs. Offers the lowest per-instance cost among all alternatives at $0.38/hr, providing ~10.4% savings per instance. AMD EPYC processors handle compute-heavy Celery workloads effectively with negligible performance difference for most task types.

Newer-generation AMD instance (Zen 3) at nearly the same price as c5a.2xlarge. Offers improved per-core performance over c5a, which could translate to slightly faster task processing and marginally fewer instances needed. Savings of ~10% per instance with a generational performance uplift.
Current baseline instance type. No migration effort required. Recommended as fallback if AMD compatibility has not been validated for the beautify_v4 workload.

rationale.scaling_policy: The policy is redesigned around the observed queue depth distribution. The median queue depth is ~1,547 messages and the average is ~2,379, so the neutral/low-growth zone is set around 500-1,500 messages to avoid unnecessary scaling during normal load. Aggressive scale-down steps at 0-50 (adjustment -50) and 50-200 (adjustment -15) ensure rapid cost reduction when the queue drains, which aligns with the cost optimization strategy. The scale-up thresholds are raised compared to the current policy: meaningful scale-up only begins at 500+ messages (above the lower quartile), with progressively larger additions at 4,000+ and 10,000+ to handle the p95 (6,535) and p99 (14,019) surges. The top step (25,000+, adjustment +70) covers extreme peaks up to the observed max of ~42,827. Scale-up steps are deliberately fewer and with higher thresholds to prefer tolerating slightly longer queue latency over launching expensive capacity prematurely. The cooldown is set to 300 seconds, matching the instance_drain_seconds (the maximum of warmup=120s and drain=300s), ensuring instances fully drain before further terminations and fully warm up before further launches.
rationale.strategy_impact: Cost optimization strategy drove several key decisions: (1) Scale-down steps are aggressive with large negative adjustments (-50, -15, -5) to shed capacity quickly when demand drops, minimizing idle instance hours. (2) Scale-up thresholds are raised (starting at 500 vs the previous 150) to tolerate moderate queue buildup rather than immediately adding expensive instances. (3) The 300s cooldown prevents thrashing which wastes money on premature launches/terminations. (4) Instance recommendations prioritize the cheapest alternatives (c5a.2xlarge and c6a.2xlarge), both offering ~10% per-instance savings. At an average fleet size of ~61 instances, switching to c5a.2xlarge saves approximately $61 × $32.12/month ≈ $1,959/month. Combined with the tighter scaling policy reducing average fleet size, total monthly savings could be substantial.
rationale.risk_notes: 1) The 300s cooldown means the ASG cannot react to rapid queue spikes for 5 minutes after any scaling action. During flash surges (observed max ~42,827), this could temporarily increase queue latency. Monitor p99 task completion times after deployment. 2) The aggressive -50 scale-down at 0-50 messages could overshoot if the queue refills quickly; the min_size=1 guardrail prevents scaling to zero, but rapid oscillation between low and high capacity is possible during bursty patterns. Consider monitoring scaling event frequency. 3) Switching to c5a.2xlarge (AMD) requires validation that the beautify_v4 Python workload has no x86 Intel-specific dependencies (e.g., MKL-optimized libraries). Test thoroughly before fleet-wide rollout. 4) The observed peak desired capacity of ~159 instances is well below the max_size of 250, so the current max_size remains safe and should not be lowered. 5) Zero-depth percentage is only 1.66%, confirming the queue is almost always active—scaling to zero is not recommended.
